_doc: The Trade Ledger (core/trade.gd). Prices derive from an item's base price times a regional factor, a seasonal/festival demand and (selling only) a glut and a freshness factor. Anything not listed sits at 1.0, so every item has a price. `groups` maps zone regions to trade regions; a thing is cheap in its `home` groups and dear in its `wants` groups. Home Cheshire never gets dearer than today: no `wants` list names north_west for a Cheshire-made thing.

seasonal.note: stews are wanted in the cold
everyone wants fish by the seaside

events.wire: The boats at Lerwick have landed more herring than anyone can sell, and Aberdeen, Inverness and Stornoway are awash with it. Fish is cheap to sell in all four.
events.stall: Lerwick has landed so much herring that nobody up here will pay for any. Take it somewhere that has to go without.

events.wire: Gales are keeping the boats in at Hull, Whitby and the Tyne, and the stalls there are crying out for fish.
events.stall: Nothing has gone out of Hull for days, with this wind. If you have fish, the north east will pay for it.

events.wire: The forcing sheds of the Rhubarb Triangle are in full cry and Yorkshire is up to its ears in rhubarb. Do not bring any.
events.stall: It is rhubarb, rhubarb, rhubarb at the Yorkshire stalls this week. I would not carry coals to Newcastle, or sticks to Leeds.

events.wire: A late frost has caught the early beans and peas across the Midlands, the South and East Anglia. Anyone with a basketful of them is about to be popular.
events.stall: That frost took the beans. If you have any peas or beans in your bag, you have picked the right week.

events.wire: A wet summer has done the root crops no favours in East Anglia, the Midlands and the North East. Carrots, parsnips, leeks and spuds are short.
events.stall: Poor harvest on the root crops this year. The greengrocers over here are paying over the odds.

events.wire: A hard frost is settling on the north, and everybody wants something hot. Stews and soups are dear in the North West, the North East and Scotland.
events.stall: Everyone wants a stew this week. If you can make one, you can sell one.

events.wire: A heatwave has sent the South and Wales to the seaside, and the fish stalls cannot keep up.
events.stall: It is roasting, the beach is heaving and the fish is flying off the slab. Bring me some.

events.wire: A rail strike has been called. With nothing moving by train, every price gap between the regions has widened: what is dear is dearer and what is cheap is cheaper. Walking and boats are back in fashion.
events.stall: Rail strike, so nothing is coming in from the other end of the country. Anyone who gets a load through will do very nicely.

events.wire: The festival crowds have filled Edinburgh and the overspill is eating its way through Glasgow. Hot dinners are dear in both.
events.stall: The city is heaving with festival people, all of them hungry. Dishes are going like hot cakes.

events.wire: It is race week in Galway, and the whole town has come to eat. Dishes are dear there for a few days.
events.stall: Race week. Every bed in Galway is taken and everybody has an appetite. A proper dinner will fetch a proper price.

events.wire: The students are back in Oxford, Cambridge, Nottingham and Birmingham, and for a week or so they will pay for a dinner that is not beans on toast.
events.stall: The freshers have landed, and not one of them can cook. Dishes sell well.

events.wire: A big day at Croke Park has filled Dublin to the rafters. The stalls on Moore Street have been cleaned out of hot food.
events.stall: There is a match on at Croke Park and the whole city is out. Anything hot sells.

events.wire: The smokehouses at Arbroath are struggling to keep up, and a real Arbroath smokie is hard to find in Wales, Ireland or the Midlands.
events.stall: I cannot get a smokie for love nor money. If you have some, bring them here.

events.wire: There is a run on Welsh cakes, laverbread and cawl in the South and the Midlands, and not enough coming over the border.
events.stall: Everyone wants something Welsh at the moment, and I have run out of the lot.

asks: Mind you bring them in good time.
They are for a wedding, so no pressure.

report.monday: It's Monday, so here is the weekly market report.
report.quiet: Trading was quiet and the Money Box has nothing to say, which is the first time that has happened.
report.close: That was the Money Box. Remember, a price is only what somebody will pay, and a bargain is only what you did with it.
report.tip: %s is cheap in %s and keenly wanted in %s. Mind the train fare, and mind the glut.
